request.spec:
The sheet has a maximum of open claims per person (settings, a whole number, blank means none, not
dated; SETTING_CHANGED key=max-open value=<n>). Opening a claim, alone or by the bulk button or a
paste, is refused when the person already has that many OPEN or PENDING claims.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheet has a maximum of open claims per person (settings, a whole number, blank means none, not
dated; SETTING_CHANGED key=max-open value=<n>). Opening a claim, alone or by the bulk button or a
paste, is refused when the person already has that many OPEN or PENDING claims.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've added the max-open setting and the refusal. The main "max open claims" test and scenario 1 pass. Scenarios 2 and 3 fail, and neither can pass as the spec is written.

**What I changed**
- **Stored data:** new migration `V114__sheet_max_open.sql` adds a nullable `max_open` column to the sheet. It's also carried into the sheet's as-of-date view and into sheet clones.
- **Server:** a new endpoint saves the setting and writes `SETTING_CHANGED … key=max-open value=<n>` to the audit file, with nothing after `value=` when cleared. It accepts the same input as the review-SLA setting: a whole number or blank. The settings view now includes `maxOpen`.
- **The refusal:** `ClaimService.java` checks the limit inside `move`, the one path that every open goes through: single, bulk and paste. When the person already has that many OPEN or PENDING claims, the open is refused with an error and nothing is written. A bulk open skips just that claim and counts it as refused; a paste is refused as a whole.
- **Front end:** a settings field `setting-max-open` and the value in force, `setting-max-open-current`, wired the same way as the review-SLA setting.

Two behaviours you might not assume: an open that would go to REVIEW (claim over the review threshold) also counts as opening, so it's refused too. Bringing a claim back to OPEN by reviewing or rejecting it, or splitting one, isn't blocked; the request only covers opening.

**The failing tests**
- **Scenarios 2 and 3:** both expect `sheet-parent` to show the literal text `__SHEET__-p` (spec lines 829 and 1239). That's a placeholder that was never filled in. The app correctly shows the real id, e.g. `smvku7fch93x5-p`, so these checks can't pass. Neither scenario touches max-open.
- **Scenario 2 also fails earlier, at line 825:** an `addClaim` gets neither a new row nor an error. The audit file shows a `CLAIM_EDITED` instead of a `CLAIM_ADDED`. My guess is that the claim form stays in edit mode after the refused `editClaim` just before it, so the add is saved as an edit. That's existing claim-form behaviour, max-open isn't set in that test, and I left it alone. If you want it fixed, that's a separate change.
